decisions.reason: Fouling detection automation supports the firm's push into heat and energy recovery from wastewater and fits its automation software portfolio, so the expanding firm will likely keep it despite the niche market.
The fouling detection system complements Product A and likely stems from funded R&D, so it stays on the market, though overlap with A creates some risk of consolidation.
A spring-controlled flap weir is close to the firm's core hydraulic steelwork business for flood control and water level regulation, so withdrawal soon after launch is unlikely.
An energy management system for water facilities matches the strategic direction toward digital networking and efficiency and meets strong utility demand, so it will be kept.
The overflow flap gate line has its own website page and several models, which signals a core product the firm is actively promoting.
